title: Finite etale trivialization of a lisse sheaf
statement:
Let $X$ be of finite type over a field, let $\Lambda$ be
a finite commutative ring, and let $L$ be a
finite locally
constant $\Lambda$-module sheaf. There is a
finite etale
surjective map $p:P\to X$ such that $p^*L$ is constant
on each connected component of $P$, with a finite
$\Lambda$-module fibre. If $X$ is connected, one common
finite module can be used on all of $P$.

proof.text: The field $k$ is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0$ and $k$), and $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is quasi-compact and locally Noetherian. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], applied to the structure morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, makes $X$ Noetherian. By [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-subset-finite-components] with $E=X$, write $X=Z_1\cup\cdots\cup Z_r$ with irreducible closed $Z_i$. Each $Z_i$ is connected, so lies in one connected component. Every connected component is therefore a union of some of these finitely many $Z_i$ and is closed. There are finitely many connected components, and the complement of each is a finite union of closed components, so each is open. We work on the resulting nonempty connected open-and-closed subschemes $X_i$; if $X$ is empty, the identity of the empty scheme already satisfies the conclusion.

proof.text: Fix a connected component $X_0$ and a geometric point $\bar x\to X_0$. The finite locally constant module hypothesis means that the underlying sheaf of sets of $L|_{X_0}$ is a finite locally constant set sheaf, with finite fibre $M=L_{\bar x}$; this is the lisse/finite-stalk clause of [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. By [thm-galois-lc-etale] and [thm-galois-fundamental], finite locally constant sheaves are identified with finite sets carrying a continuous right action of $G=\pi_1(X_0,\bar x)$. Under this identification, the addition, zero, and scalar-multiplication maps of the module sheaf are maps of finite locally constant sheaves, so the induced $G$-action on $M$ is $\Lambda$-linear. Explicitly, preservation of finite products identifies the fibre of $L\times L$ with $M\times M$, and equivariance of addition and scalar multiplication gives $(m+n)g=mg+ng$ and $(am)g=a(mg)$ for $g\in G$, $a\in\Lambda$. Equivariance of zero gives $0g=0$. Thus every $g$ acts by a module automorphism.

Let $H=\{g\in G:mg=m\text{ for every }m\in M\}$ be the kernel of the action. It is a subgroup: the right-action identities show that elements fixing every $m$ are closed under products and inverses. For each $m\in M$, continuity of the finite discrete action from [thm-galois-fundamental] makes $\{g:mg=m\}$ open (it is the inverse image of $\{m\}$ under $g\mapsto mg$). The finite intersection of these stabilizers is $H$, so $H$ is open.

By the pointed clause of [cor-galois-open-subgroups], $H$ corresponds to a nonempty connected finite etale morphism $p_0:P_0\to X_0$ with a chosen point of its geometric fibre whose stabilizer is exactly $H$. By the finite-etale base-change clause of [thm-galois-fundamental], $(p_0)_*$ identifies $\pi_1(P_0)$ with this stabilizer. Base-change compatibility in [thm-galois-lc-etale] and [thm-galois-fundamental] consequently identifies $p_0^*L$ with the restricted $H$-action on $M$. This action is trivial by step 3. The constant set sheaf $\underline M$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] is the finite coproduct, indexed by $M$, of the terminal sheaf: this follows by sheafifying the corresponding coproduct of constant singleton presheaves. Since the equivalence preserves finite colimits and terminal objects, its action on the fibre of $\underline M$ is the trivial action on $M$. Full faithfulness therefore gives a unique isomorphism of underlying set sheaves inducing the identity on $M$. Under this isomorphism, addition, zero and each scalar operation agree with the constant operations: their fibre maps are respectively $(m,n)\mapsto m+n$, $0$, and $m\mapsto am$, and faithfulness, with preservation of products, makes the corresponding sheaf maps equal. Hence $p_0^*L\cong\underline M$ as module sheaves, without assuming that $M$ is free.

The degree clause of [cor-galois-open-subgroups] says that $p_0$ has constant finite locally free degree $d=[G:H]\geq1$. By [def-pc-finite-locally-free], for every point $y\in X_0$ the global-section algebra of the fibre has dimension $d$ over $\kappa(y)$. The empty scheme has the zero global-section algebra, of dimension zero, so this fibre cannot be empty. Thus every $y$ has a preimage and $p_0$ is surjective. Form $P=\coprod_iP_i$ using [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], and define $p:P\to X$ by the maps $P_i\to X_i\hookrightarrow X$. Its restriction over the open-and-closed $X_i$ is precisely $p_i$, since the coproduct summands have disjoint images. Hence $p$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-local-on-target]. For etaleness, use the affine-local characterization included in [def-weil-etale-morphism]: every affine source/target chart witnessing etaleness of $P_i\to X_i$ is also a chart in the open subschemes $P_i\subset P$ and $X_i\subset X$; these charts cover $P$, so $p$ is etale. It is surjective because all the $p_i$ are surjective. Each $P_i$ is connected and open and closed, so these are the connected components of $P$, and step 4 gives the required constant module sheaf on each. If $X$ is connected there is one $X_i$, so the same finite module $M$ serves all of $P$.

lean.statement: theorem exists_finite_etale_surjective_trivializing_lisse (k : Type u) [Field k] (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ] [Finite Λ] (L : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)) (hL : Scheme.IsFiniteLocallyConstantSheaf L) : ∃ (P : Scheme.{u}) (p : P ⟶ X), IsFinite p ∧ Etale p ∧ Surjective p ∧ (∀ (x : P), ∃ U : P.Opens, (U : Set P) = connectedComponent x ∧ ∃ M : ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ, Finite M ∧ Nonempty ((Etale.upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) U.ι).obj ((Etale.upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) p).obj L) ≅ (constantSheaf U.toScheme.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)).obj M)) ∧ (ConnectedSpace X → ∃ (M : ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ), Finite M ∧ Nonempty ((Etale.upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) p).obj L ≅ (constantSheaf P.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)).obj M))
lean.note: Lisse uses the recorded transitive dependency Scheme.IsFiniteLocallyConstantSheaf at ModuleCat Λ. Components are encoded by opens with underlying set connectedComponent x. The connected-base clause uses one constant module on all of P.
